one_month_reasoning: Window 2026-10-02 to 2026-10-31. A mid-October September production update is still likely (the Aug-26 6-K moved only the infrastructure section to quarterly); with hashprice ~$39/PH/day it should read fine but it is largely known. Q3 results (~Nov 9-18) fall outside the window. No lock-up or index event identified. The drivers are BTC beta (~$84.8k) and financing headlines (the $1B ATM has barely been used, $8.4M by 9/29, so sales could pick up; Tydal project debt; current BIT loans), which tilt slightly negative, against ~25% short interest. So I stay near-symmetric: lognormal median $10.45, monthly sigma ~30% (108%/3.5). Unchanged in rounds 3 and 4: the GPU-life work, the site-by-site rebuild and the split discount rate concern long-run value, not this window; the 9/29 A201 announcement and the 9/14 A202 facility are already in the 10/1 close.

fair_value.method: Blend of the split-rate site-by-site DCF ($1.63, 35%), SOTP ($4.81, 40%) and EV/NTM sales ($8.73, 25%) = $4.68, rounded $4.7. Round 4: every one of the 20 inventory sites is valued once (A202 added as a cost-bearing GPU-cloud option, Tydal P3, Knoxville, Wenatchee, Fox Creek, Massillon +47 MW, Clarington, Weathersfield added probability-weighted net of capex; Rockdale HPC moved onto the 179 MW expansion); contracted cash flows discounted at 8.0-11.0% by counterparty and credit support, everything else at 12.5% (single-rate DCF $1.04); the 2032 notes held as debt (277M shares).

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Site-by-site DCF valued 2026-10-01, rolled forward 12 months at 15%. Split-rate (used in the blend): Tydal P1-2 $902M net of $500M capex (PV of rent $755M in the LC-backed years at 8.0%, $448M in years 6-10 at 10.5%, $187M in years 11-16 at 12.5%); A101 $50M; legacy fleet $47M; A102 $84M; A201 $150M (80% x $225M contracted case + 20% x -$152M); A202 $64M; Knoxville $82M; Wenatchee $10M; mining sites $951M (Rockdale 563 MW $364M, Jigmeling $324M, Massillon 174 MW $113M, Gedu $65M, Molde $54M, Oromia $32M); Massillon +47 MW $19M; Fox Creek $6M; Rockdale +179 MW lease option $18M; Tydal P3 $51M; Clarington $14M; Weathersfield $9M; Gelephu $0; Sparks/R&D -$601M. EV $1,858M - net debt $1,465M = $393M / 277M = $1.42 x 1.15 = $1.63. Single-rate (all at 12.5%): EV $1,715M -> $1.04. GPU life 5/6/7 yrs: $1.68/$1.63/$1.73.

R&D) split into mining ex-R&D $1,007M allocated by MW over 1,557 MW (six energized mining sites + Knoxville's former mining load) and corporate/SEALMINER R&D (-$581M) assigned to the Sparks row. Equity = EV - net debt $1,465M = $393M / 277M = $1.42, x1.15 roll-forward = $1.63 (single-rate $0.90 -> $1.04)

$4.7B / sum of 1.03^t, t=0..15 (20.16) = $233M. Source conflict: written disclosures keep Phase 1 at 2026-12-31 and Phase 2 at 2027-03-31; I keep the CEO's later, more specific Q2-call statement (single phase at the Phase 2 date), which costs at most ~$29M of rent

inputs_detail.input: Tydal cash conversion, walk, default, completion
inputs_detail.value: Cash = 79.2% of rent (90% NOI - 2% maintenance, 10% tax); 3% completion haircut; 10% Volta default from lease year 6 with no re-let; 35% no-fee walk at year 10; remaining capex $500M
inputs_detail.derivation: Replaces round 3's flat 8% haircut with an explicit default leg (inventory flag 13): the reported end-customer deal behind Volta (Anthropic, ~6 yrs, press only) ends around lease year 6, and the ~$1.3B LCs (~5 years of rent) are 'anticipated' and conditional. Capex $500M per the Tydal 6-K/inventory (round 3 used $450M)

No Bitdeer debt is priced against any contract (inventory), and its only secured debt is the related-party BIT loan at 13.0% effective. Market anchors for secured project debt on HPC leases: AWS-tenant 6.0% (Cipher Stingray), IG-offtake GPU loans SOFR+2.25-2.50% / 5.96% (IREN-Microsoft) / 6.78% (Lambda), Google-backstopped Fluidstack leases 7.125% (Cipher) and 7.75% (TeraWulf), unrated customers SOFR+5.50% (CoreWeave DDTL 5.5) and 9.25% for CoreWeave-tenant notes (Applied Digital). Tydal years 1-5 are covered by ~$1.3B of AA-range bank LCs (~5 years of rent): 7.75% Google-backstop anchor +~25bp because the LCs are still conditional and the halls unfinished = 8.0%. Years 6-10 rest on Volta alone (private, unrated, end-customer deal ~6 yrs): unrated-customer anchor ~9.5-10% + 50-100bp = 10.5%. Years 11-16 are terminable by the tenant at no fee, so they are optional for the tenant and stay at WACC. A102: undisclosed customers but prepayments cover >50% of capex: 10.5%. A201/A101: undisclosed counterparties, no executed agreements or deposits disclosed for A201: 11.0%
Unchanged from round 3: cost of equity ~15.3% = 5.29% + beta ~2.0 x 5% ERP; pre-tax debt ~8% blend; ~60/40

methods.name: SOTP
methods.inputs: At 2027-10-01: Tydal $1.52B (split-rate, default leg, 3% haircut) + contracted AI cloud $0.81B (fleet $34M, A102 $179M, A201 80%-weighted $593M) + AI pipeline $0.18B (A202, Knoxville, Wenatchee at DCF value net of capex, rolled forward) + mining $0.66B + powered-land pipeline $0.38B (959 MW x $0.4M/MW: Rockdale +179, Clarington 570 at 50% for litigation, Weathersfield 300, Fox Creek 101, Massillon +47, Tydal P3 47) + SEALMINER net of R&D $0 = EV $3.55B; less forward net debt $2.215B; / 277M = $4.81.

A202 $64M + Knoxville $82M + Wenatchee $10M (probability-weighted, net of GPU and conversion capex, A202 fee charged) x 1.125. These MW are not also counted as powered land

Round-3 $1,760M + $375M 2032 notes at face + $50M Tydal remaining capex at the inventory's ~$500M (was $450M) - ~$30M more A201 prepayment (80% vs 65% conversion) + ~$40M less A201 EBITDA before the horizon (revenue from ~Jul-2027, not Q2: supervisor) + ~$20M remaining Sparks plant capex. Pipeline AI capex (A202, Knoxville, Wenatchee) is not added here because those sites enter at values already net of their capex

bear.story: BTC slides toward $65-70k and hashprice under $30 into the April-2028 halving; Volta misses a credit-backstop milestone or the LCs are not issued, so the Tydal years 6-10 look unbacked and the market discounts the whole lease near my WACC; A201 commitments do not convert, leaving ~$563M of GB300 racks on falling spot prices (~-$150M NPV); A202 stays empty while Bitdeer pays ~$94M/yr for the facility; BIT loans roll at 13% and the ATM is used below $8. Lower than round 3's $3.8 because the 2032 notes are debt and A202 is a cost.

base.story: Tydal commences around 2027-04-01 with the LCs in place and gets project debt near the 7-8% market for backstopped leases; A102 bills from Q1-2027 and A201 mostly converts; A202 finds partial offtake; hashprice holds high-$30s into 2027. Fundamental value ~$4.7, but the market keeps paying for ~$2.9B of AI backlog and 3 GW of power, so the stock trades between fair value and spot with 5-10% dilution.

bull.story: A second large HPC lease (Rockdale expansion or Tydal P3) with an investment-grade-backed tenant, A202 sold out at A102-like pricing, BTC above $110k; the 2032 notes convert; rerating toward contracted-HPC multiples and short covering push toward the ~$22 consensus target.

thesis_break_reason: At ~$4.00 the market cap (~$1.11B on 277M diluted shares) roughly equals my split-rate value of the contracted book alone (Tydal $902M net of capex + A102 $84M + A201 $150M = $1.14B), so the market would be valuing the mining fleet, the GPU fleet, 1.4 GW of pipeline and the R&D drag at exactly net debt (~$1.47B with converts at face). Getting there would most likely take a Volta credit-backstop failure or Tydal delay, A201 commitments failing with the racks bought, A202 left empty under its 10-year fee, a squeeze on the BIT loans at 13%, or deeply dilutive equity. Cut from $4.50 because the notes are now debt and the default leg and split rate lower Tydal; still above my $3.4 bear case.

reasoning: Round 4 (site coverage and split discounting). (1) Sites: I rebuilt the DCF from the 20-row inventory so each site appears once. Fixes to my flags: A202 (flag 2) is now a GPU-cloud option in which Bitdeer is the customer paying a 10-year fee: 35% contracted at RFS, 25% a year later, 40% never (fee half mitigated), worth +$64M; Tydal P3 (flag 7) 45% lease, $51M; Knoxville/Wenatchee (flag 8) 35%/30% GPU cloud with conversion and GPU capex, else back to mining, $82M/$10M; the Rockdale lease option (flag 10) now sits on the 179 MW expansion, so it no longer shares power with the 563 MW mining fleet, at 25% (from 30%) and at WACC, $18M; Fox Creek and Massillon +47 MW (flag 14) added as mining, $6M/$19M; Clarington and Weathersfield as probability-weighted leases, $14M/$9M; Gelephu LOI at zero; A201 (flags 4, 16) at 80% on 128 racks; Tydal (flag 13) now has a 10% default leg at year 6, when the reported end-customer deal ends; Sparks carries the R&D drag. I disagree with the inventory on one fact: the 9/29 A201 release (checked) says 'off-take commitments', not signed or executed. (2) Discounting: no contract-level debt is priced, so I anchored on the market for secured debt against HPC leases (6.0-7.75% for IG or Google-backed tenants, ~9.25-10% for unrated ones; CCIR: IG +225-250bp vs unrated +550bp). Tydal years 1-5 (LC-backed) at 8.0%, years 6-10 at 10.5%, years 11-16 (tenant can walk free) at 12.5%; A102 at 10.5%, A201/A101 at 11%. Split-rate DCF $1.63 vs single-rate (all 12.5%) $1.04. (3) Supervisor corrections: 2032 notes as debt (277M shares), A201 revenue from Jul-2027, and the CoinShares definition stated. Round-3 DCF $2.79 -> $1.61 with the notes as debt -> $1.63: the new sites (+$0.95/sh before roll) roughly offset the Tydal default leg, $500M capex and split rates (-$0.6), and A202's fee. GPU life (CoreWeave 6, Nebius 5, IREN 5 verified in IREN's FY26 10-K) left at a 6-yr base; 5/7 yrs give $1.68/$1.73. SOTP $5.33 -> $4.81 (notes as debt, site-by-site pipeline); EV/sales $8.79 -> $8.73. Blend $5.3 -> $4.7. Ladder: same rule (median at 35% of the log-gap to fair value, sigma 0.80, 4% distress): median ~$7.99, P(>=$10.64) 0.346. Research this round: 3 searches, 6 fetches (A201 release, Applied Digital 8-K, CCIR tracker, colocation pricing, EDGAR full-text search, IREN 10-K R68).

gpu_life.revenue_decay_path: Contracted GPUs (A102, 70% of A201, half the existing fleet for ~2 yrs) at contract price for the term; then or if uncontracted, revenue index by age vs launch price 1.00/0.72/0.52/0.45/0.40/0.35 (about -50% within ~2 yrs of the successor, then ~-10%/yr), uncontracted utilisation 85%; retired after year 6 with 9% salvage; tail would stay cash-positive to ~year 8 (break-even index ~0.25 vs power/colo/site cost at 18% of launch revenue). 5-yr: 1.00/0.65/0.45/0.38/0.33, salvage 12%, Tydal walk 45%; 7-yr: 1.00/0.78/0.60/0.52/0.46/0.41/0.36, salvage 6%, walk 30%. Applied unchanged to A202, Knoxville and Wenatchee (now modelled); pipeline contract case priced at 90% of A102 per MW.
gpu_life.note: Split-rate DCF with the notes as debt. Life barely moves value: the year-6 tail is near cash-neutral (index 0.35 against fixed direct costs), so the 5-yr case (12% salvage a year earlier) ends slightly above the 6-yr base even with the Tydal walk at 45%. Company lives after the fact-check: CoreWeave 6, Nebius 5 (from 1 Jan 2026), IREN 5 (verified, FY26 10-K R68), Lambda 5. I keep 6 because Bitdeer's GPUs are on 5-yr contracts plus a low-priced tail, but the median company life is 5.

discounting.basis: Contracted tiers: Tydal lease years 1-5 (~$1.24B of rent, roughly matched by the ~$1.3B bank LCs) at 8.0% = Google-backstopped Fluidstack lease notes at 7.125-7.75% (Cipher, TeraWulf) + ~25bp because the LCs are 'anticipated' and the halls are unfinished; Tydal years 6-10 (Volta-only credit, unrated, reported end-customer deal ~6 yrs) at 10.5% = unrated-customer GPU debt at SOFR+5.50% / CoreWeave-tenant notes at 9.25% + 50-100bp; Tydal years 11-16 at WACC because the tenant can walk free at year 10; A102 at 10.5% (undisclosed customers, >50% of capex prepaid); A201 and A101 at 11.0% (undisclosed, A201 not shown as executed). Bitdeer has no priced debt against any contract; its only secured debt is the related-party BIT loan at 13.0% effective, above my WACC's debt leg, so it is not the anchor. Uncontracted, post-contract, pipeline, mining, R&D and terminal flows at the 12.5% WACC; the A202 facility fee (a fixed obligation) at 9%. Single-rate = every cash flow at 12.5%. Both are per share at 2027-10-01 on 277M shares with the notes as debt; round 3's own structure (Tydal 9%, notes as debt) gave $1.61. site_coverage value_per_share = each site's split-rate PV at 2026-10-01 / 277M shares (EV contribution before net debt of $5.29/sh); sum $6.71/sh, less net debt, x1.15 roll-forward = the $1.63 DCF.
